title: Cotton Bowl, Dec. 2020: OU Routs Florida 55-20 With 684 Yards
question: Who won the Cotton Bowl between Oklahoma and Florida in December 2020?
answer: Oklahoma beat Florida 55-20 in the Cotton Bowl on December 30, 2020, in Arlington, Texas. The Sooners' 55 points and 684 total yards were the most they had ever produced in a bowl game.
summary: Oklahoma beat Florida 55-20 in the Dec. 30, 2020 Cotton Bowl, rushing for 435 yards and setting school bowl highs for points and total yards (684).
body: After three straight playoff semifinal losses, Oklahoma finally closed a season with a New Year's Six win. Lincoln Riley's Sooners, sixth in the final CFP rankings and fresh off a sixth straight Big 12 title, met SEC runner-up Florida and Heisman finalist Kyle Trask on December 30, 2020, in the first New Year's Six game of that bowl season.

OU led 17-0 within the first seven minutes. Spencer Rattler hit fellow freshman Marvin Mims for a 27-yard touchdown on the opening drive, and Tre Norwood returned an interception 45 yards for a score on Florida's first possession. Trask threw three interceptions in the first quarter after throwing only five all season.

Then the ground game took over. Rhamondre Stevenson ran for 186 yards, freshman Marcus Major added 110, and Oklahoma finished with 435 rushing yards, a Cotton Bowl record. The Sooners' 55 points and 684 total yards were the most in any OU bowl game, per the AP, and the 684 yards also set a Cotton Bowl mark. Rattler threw three touchdown passes and ran for another. Stevenson and Norwood were named the offensive and defensive MVPs.

Florida was short-handed, with 17 players unavailable, including star tight end Kyle Pitts, who opted out. The win finished an eight-game winning streak for the 9-2 Sooners, who played it in AT&T Stadium, the same building where they had won the Big 12 title 11 days earlier.
